Harry Kane is set to become England's most-capped player ever on Thursday night - will it also be time to crown him the country's greatest? Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph last month coronated him as the world's best for the past year. Whether he should have the all-time No 1 spot for his country makes for a fascinating debate - not least with the weight of a World Cup win on the side of historic icons such as Bobby Charlton (another Ballon d'Or winner) and Bobby Moore (another captain fantastic). But, minus the big team triumph, Kane's individual case is compelling. metadata.summary: Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.
metadata.content: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino: Would Argentine be the perfect fit or just another manager to fall foul of Old Trafford chaos? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino: Would Argentine be the perfect fit or just another manager to fall foul of Old Trafford chaos? Manchester United are close to agreeing a deal with Mauricio Pochettino if Michael Carrick is sacked; can it be third time lucky in the Premier League for the Argentine? Or is this move, as has proved with others, doomed to fail from the start? Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Wednesday 11 November 2026 09:24, UK Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge. Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances? The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at PSG was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League, but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea. All along this journey of complicated courtship United were at play. metadata.summary: Williams team principal James Vowles has admitted his squad "got carried away" with their success last season but insists a disappointing 2026 campaign is merely "a blip".
metadata.content: James Vowles: Williams boss admits team got carried away with success but says 2026 F1 season struggles are only 'a blip' | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content James Vowles: Williams boss admits team got carried away with success but says 2026 F1 season struggles are only 'a blip' Watch or listen to the latest episode of The Fast and the Curious to hear Williams boss James Vowles discuss the team's 2026 struggles, why he is confident a corner has been turned, and the changes he wants to see made to F1's cost cap rules Tuesday 10 November 2026 19:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joining Christian Hewgil on the Fast and the Curious podcast, Williams Team Principal James Vowles responds to comments on the pressure of his position. Williams team principal James Vowles has admitted his squad "got carried away" with their success last season but insists a disappointing 2026 campaign is merely "a blip". Vowles took charge of Williams after joining from Mercedes at the start of 2023 and appeared to be having a hugely positive impact when the team finished fifth in the 2025 constructors' standings, which was their best finish since 2017. However, the biggest regulation change in the sport's history, which saw the introduction of both new power units and chassis, has seen Williams regress, leaving drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon hugely frustrated.
